title: How to spot a fake natty: they don't understand programming
summary: NH argues that the surest sign of a fake natural is dismissing programming principles. Enhanced lifters push volume and pump work without relevant intensity, avoid heavy compounds, and never have to think about frequency, because drugs cover what naturals must manage through intelligent volume, intensity and frequency.
claims: Physical markers like traps and jaw can indicate drug use but are not 100% reliable, and are often used by people who don't want to do the work
Programming is everything in natural bodybuilding; volume, intensity and frequency cannot be ignored
A big guy who says volume, intensity and frequency don't matter is probably enhanced: he has the answers but cannot show the equation
Enhanced lifters overvalue volume and pump while ignoring the intensity window it happens in, e.g. benching 225 forever with a wide grip; for naturals that is junk volume
Some junk volume is fine if relevant intensity windows elsewhere pick up the slack, but enhanced lifters' programs are all junk volume
Explaining natural vs enhanced frequency differences through protein synthesis is not precise enough
Naturals need to train the lower body often, at least three times a week; he trains it every two days on an upper/lower split
Destroying legs once a week is awful advice for naturals: extreme soreness, resentment of leg day, a week of recovery and fewer gains
Naturals must lift heavy relative to their strength: it puts you in relevant intensity windows, gives high-quality tonnage in little time, and builds strength that drives volume and progression
Enhanced lifters can grow staying around 60% intensity and never pushing; naturals get every inch of size from training
The holy trinity of fake-natty nonsense: volume with no intensity window, avoiding intensity and compound lifts (claiming machines and cables are enough), and not understanding frequency
Taking advice from an enhanced lifter is like learning chess from someone whose opponent lets them win; without drugs those three variables run out of control
The halo effect makes people assume big means knowledgeable; he has no exercise science degree himself but can discuss programming for hours
